submission.name: GrantRoute
submission.tagline: A quick guide to the next step when a small organization handles a payment.
submission.inspiration: Student clubs and neighborhood groups often make purchases with limited budgets and confusing payment options. We wanted to help a treasurer quickly compare likely benefits and keep a short explanation beside the decision.
submission.what_it_does: The prototype lets a user choose a purchase category and compare example cards or payment methods against a small rewards table. Gemini can turn the comparison into a plain-language summary, and ElevenLabs can read that summary aloud. Account linking and recommendations are still mocked, so the demo uses sample organization profiles and card data.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used a React and Next.js interface with a small backend that looks up reward rules from JSON data. A Gemini request drafts a short explanation from the selected category and matching rates, while ElevenLabs converts the explanation to speech. Plaid Sandbox account retrieval was explored separately, but it is not connected to the recommendation flow yet.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Getting reliable location or merchant context proved difficult, and our example reward rules cover only a narrow set of cards. The account connection and recommendation pieces are not joined, so a user still has to choose from sample data rather than their actual accounts.
submission.accomplishments: We made a compact comparison screen and demonstrated a spoken explanation of why one sample option might fit a purchase. The prototype focuses on making the decision understandable for a group treasurer rather than only showing a multiplier.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that an apparent reward rate is only useful when the merchant category and card rules line up. AI can make a comparison easier to explain, but it cannot fix missing or stale rewards data.
submission.whats_next: We would connect account retrieval, expand the rules database, and let organizations save purchase policies for future treasurers. We would also add clearer checks for fees and other conditions before presenting a recommendation.
